findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no topic_users row
findings.body: Line 105 does `TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])`, which returns nil when the logged-in user has no row for this topic (they never visited or read it, or the link was opened while logged in as an account with no relation to the topic). Line 107 then calls `tu.notification_level` and raises NoMethodError, producing a 500. Use `TopicUser.change` (which creates the row when missing) or handle the nil case explicitly.

findings.title: tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change and can be silently undone by auto-tracking
findings.body: The notification level is written with a direct `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change(...)`. `change` sets `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) and `notifications_changed_at`; this path sets neither and publishes no MessageBus `notification_level_change`. Consequence: when `notifications_reason_id` is NULL (common for rows created by reading, via the INSERT in `update_last_read`), `TopicUser.update_last_read` sets the level back to tracking once enough reading time accumulates, and `TopicUser.auto_track` does the same on new posts. The user's unsubscribe is silently reverted. Fix by calling `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)`.

findings.title: Unsubscribe leaves watching/tracking users at 'regular', which still sends reply and mention emails
findings.body: The toggle sets watching/tracking topics to `regular` and only sets `muted` when the level is already `regular` or lower. `regular` still generates reply, quote and mention notifications and emails, so a user who clicks the one-click unsubscribe link on a watched or tracked topic keeps receiving email for that topic. The new page text (`topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications`: 'You will stop receiving notifications for ...') is therefore false for those users, and they need a second click. The action should mute the topic from any level, or the copy must change.

findings.title: State-changing action exposed over GET and authenticated only by session cookie
findings.body: `unsubscribe` changes the user's notification level on a GET request (routes.rb lines 440-441). Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, so any cross-site GET to `/t/:id/unsubscribe` (for example an `` or link) performs the change for a logged-in visitor, and link prefetchers that carry the session do the same. Use a POST from a confirmation page, or a signed per-user token like the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` flow.

findings.title: Email unsubscribe link carries no recipient identity; it acts on whichever session is logged in
findings.body: The per-topic unsubscribe link in the email contains only the topic path, with no token identifying the recipient. The action uses `current_user` only. Consequences: (a) a recipient who is not logged in is redirected to login by `ensure_logged_in`, and the unsubscribe intent is lost, which is the common case for email clicks; (b) if the browser is logged in as a different account, that account's topic setting is changed while the actual recipient stays subscribed. The existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` route avoids this with a signed key; the topic link should do the same.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires :unsubscribe_url; other callers with add_unsubscribe_link will raise
findings.body: `server.en.yml` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` in `unsubscribe_link`. This line (and the same key in `body`, line 90) passes `template_args`, which only contains `unsubscribe_url` if the caller supplied it. Any caller that passes `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url` (only `send_notification_email` is updated in this PR; plugins or other mailers may call it too) will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` while building the email. Either default the value in `MessageBuilder` or guard the interpolation.

findings.title: No specs for the new unsubscribe action, Topic#unsubscribe_url, or the topic link in emails
findings.body: The new `unsubscribe` action has no controller spec. Untested paths include: the nil TopicUser case, the level transitions (regular to muted, tracking to regular), the login requirement, the slug-mismatch 301 redirect, and the rendered page. `Topic#unsubscribe_url` is untested. The only spec change adds an `unsubscribe_url:` argument to an existing test that checks only that the List-Unsubscribe header is present; no test checks that the email body contains the topic-specific link.

findings.title: Unrelated route reordering and removed constraints bundled into the feature
findings.body: The diff reorders the `moderator-liked` and `summary` routes and removes `post_number: /\d+/` from both `summary` routes. None of this is needed for the unsubscribe feature and the PR does not explain it. Dropping constraints from existing routes can change which requests match, so it should be split out or justified.

findings.title: Top-level topicUnsubscribe route paired with a nested-style template path
findings.body: The route is declared at top level as `topicUnsubscribe`, but its template is `templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, the name a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route would use. Ember resolves a route's template from its route name, so this template may not be picked up and the page could render without its content. Worth verifying in the browser, or setting `templateName` explicitly.
